subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept this narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool routing surface now, or require the broader federation identity/scope contract before adding core cross-Gateway messaging?
rationale: This PR is not only a mechanical tool change; it creates a new core config, credential, message-delivery, and session-state path across Gateway trust boundaries.

options.title: Define federation contract first
options.body: Keep this PR open or ask for a replacement after maintainers define peer identity, operator scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-history semantics.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow peer path
options.body: Explicitly accept `gateway.peers` as the product direction, then require the blocking fixes, conflict resolution, docs, security review, and real multi-Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to external bridge patterns
options.body: If native federation is out of scope, document supported plugin or operator-built bridge patterns and close implementation work only after that decision is explicit.

recommendation.title: Define federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open or ask for a replacement after maintainers define peer identity, operator scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-history semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership signals are strongest on the session tool and Gateway protocol/auth files affected by this decision.
